name: Ben-hadad
overview: Ben-hadad II was a male king of Aram, identified as the son of Hazael. His reign is noted in the biblical record specifically in 2 Kings 13:3. Beyond his royal status and lineage, Scripture does not provide further tribal or personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Ben-hadad means 'son of Hadad,' reflecting a common Semitic theophoric naming practice that acknowledges the storm god Hadad. This proper name is not indicated as being given by God but serves as a traditional personal name in the Aramean context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ben-hadad is the son of Hazael, establishing a direct familial link within the royal house of Aram. No other family relationships are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Ben-hadad II's significance lies primarily in his role as king of Aram during a period of interaction with Israel. His identification as Hazael's son situates him within a dynastic succession, which has implications for understanding the geopolitical and prophetic narrative in the biblical history. This connection underscores the continuity of Aramean leadership during the events recorded in 2 Kings.
